proposal.hypothesis: Correct two-target-per-thread trials at 96 and 128 threads measured 0.002554 s and 0.002585 s, respectively, both slower than the 0.001844 s baseline; three- and four-target trials at 128 threads were slower still. Test a five-warp, 160-thread block while keeping two targets per thread and source-register reuse fixed. The intermediate 320-target group may trade fewer CTAs against block scheduling and occupancy; no speedup is assumed.

retained: Set block=160 and items_per_block=320, with shared_memory_bytes=0.
Retain the kernel's explicit two-target mapping: each thread covers target offsets threadIdx.x and blockDim.x within a 320-target block group.
Retain independent tail guards and writes for each target, reusing each loaded source value across both target accumulations.
